pages.lesson:
LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: DESCRIPTIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing 3.2 Guided Writing: Neatness and Legibility (2 Sessions) • Handwriting •
Topic 3.4: Guided Writing: Descriptive Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing: Descriptive Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you manage your time well?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. apply basic descriptive words in writing a simple paragraph
2. appreciate the skill of writing to express feeling and opinion

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING: DESCRIPTIVE WRITING
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Writing: Descriptive Writing helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED WRITING: DESCRIPTIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Apply basic descriptive words in writing a simple paragraph

What this means
In this part you learn to apply basic descriptive words in writing a simple paragraph. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply basic descriptive words in writing a simple paragraph.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Descriptive Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply basic descriptive words in writing a simple paragraph. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the skill of writing to express feeling and opinion

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the skill of writing to express feeling and opinion. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the skill of writing to express feeling and opinion.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing: Descriptive Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the skill of writing to express feeling and opinion. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Writing: Descriptive Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Descriptive Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: apply basic descriptive words in writing a simple paragraph)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing: Descriptive Writing to a partner. (skill: appreciate the skill of writing to express feeling and opinion)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Writing: Descriptive Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: apply basic descriptive words in writing a simple paragraph.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the skill of writing to express feeling and opinion.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Writing: Descriptive Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Writing: Descriptive Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Guided Writing: Descriptive Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you manage your time well?
2. Why do we organise ideas in a paragraph?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Writing: Descriptive Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: apply basic descriptive words in writing a simple paragraph.
5. Be able to: appreciate the skill of writing to express feeling and opinion.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
